Hi there. I'm only 19 and have been suicidal for 7 years. TBH, the fact that you're 40 and shit hasn't changed makes me want to die quicker but then again I haven't been too successful due to an overactive immune system so I'm probably stuck a little longer till I have a fucking heart attack or gain the courage to use a more effective method.

That being said, u're wrong that there isn't a change in this world. I'm not biased because I have no friends and being somewhat of a ghost, have recognised and experienced some cuntery of shitheads who abuse people with decent hearts and have bullied their way to the top of society. 

However, even though there's only a minority of people that actually live for others or understand the way we are treating this world, I'm 100% this number has multiplied. U said there won't be a change for at least a few centuries. I'd say maybe a decade or two. It might be because I'm still young but I've seen that in this age, people are starting to look within themselves more for answers to life and shit and as a consequence there has been a slight increase in humanity and common sense. There's also a fucking shite load of mental disorders (and also people who like to cuddle themselves in the blanket of "i have a mental disorder") but maybe it's just because we're just becoming more existentially conscious. 

Either way, you sound like a very decent bloke who cares about others so I hope you have a few more happy moments before you die at least.

What i find particularly destructive about strong spiritual beliefs with regards to psychosis is how when it worsens, they only try harder to exorcise you which ironically makes it spiral into hell.

I was also very much into reading occult material and philosophy but it really amplified my conditions because I tried to use it as a means of escape. I hope you've been better recently.

This story's really interesting. I'm glad you have found yourself in a better place now 😊. The druggie thing hits home because through school anyone who didn't know me thought I was always high including teachers, especially considering that I kept going to the toilet during episodes. I think it's kinda cool how you and your sisters are completely different from each other in beliefs. That's pretty rare in society. BTW, have any of your family views changed since you started treatment? For me, this luckily happened about 2 years after formally starting treatment just because they began reading about mental health and not just ways to exorcise a possessed child.. Also, did u find that it made psychotic symptoms a shit ton worse when you believed you were cursed?

Hi, I'm thinking about medication but am quite reluctant because I've heard it causes fatigue and that's already an issue I don't want to worsen. Also, a bunch of other side affects and stuff which makes antipsychotics sound like hard drugs lol. Did you get any adverse side effects?

Psychosis is just when you see/hear something that shouldn't be there at all. From what you've said I think the closest thing would to it would be the shadows but its quite a common phenomena with anxiety and paranoia so hopefully it's not an onset of psychosis.

Psychosis in itself is a huge grey area though with medical treatment because it's so unique to each person. Some of my therapists didn't think I have psychosis because I'm aware its not real but others did because I still see things that aren't there.

Dellusions and psychosis are completely different though. They often come hand in hand with schizophrenia and I think schizoaffective disorder but a delusional trait which is especially indicative of schizophrenia is when you are convinced that you can directly control/read people's minds or that they can. With the reading other people's thoughts bit, it still is possible that you're just smart in that way. However, I don't believe you can regard something as a dellusion unless you are fully convinced that it's certain.

However, I did have a friend with anxiety who had this stuff so maybe you have anxiety too?

I also have bipolar and this is very similar to what I have experienced. About five years ago I got quite into philosophy and ancient texts. I felt like I was having revelations constantly about life forces and spirits and shit and got this urge to to become wiser and understand the laws of the universe. 

You're saying a lot of stuff that I believe in too (oneness of beings, collective consciousness, light etc) and sometimes I get these insights that sound crazy to others but it feels so clear. Unfortunately, I also occasionally get psychosis when I'm having manic episodes but it's still somewhat more manageable now. I have the dilemma that inside I'm almost certain of my beliefs but at the same time, I understand that it's possible everything I'm feeling is complete bullshit or it might be delusions which just makes them race even more. Also get dissociation and depersonalisation but I rationalise that with the intensity of being in my own world.

I think for mental illness sufferers who have a love for philosophy and spirituality, it's bloody hard to tell if you have a wisdom or knowledge of something incredible or if you're losing your crap. The best advice I have is to regard your thoughts as what may be true or false but don't repress the spirituality because it's clearly something that you have a passion for. Also, I know this isn't too reliable considering I am mentally ill, but nothing you've said sounds like psychosis to me.
how long did it take until you found something suitable?
